message: `|| true` turns any failure of the command before it into success and destroys the error signal; let the command fail, or stop with `|| exit 1`
help: drop the `|| true` and let the command fail, or stop on the failure: `cmd || exit 1`; if the failure is expected, test for its cause first: `test -e stale.lock && rm stale.lock`
notes: `|| true` hides the exit status the next step or the caller needs to know the work failed (REQ-KS-012)
any right-hand side of `||` whose status is always 0 does the same: `:`, `exit 0`, `! false`, a constant-true `test`, a pipeline with a `true` stage, a loop whose body always ends with status 0
